newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: South Korean prosecutors arrest Hanbo founder.
newsitem.headline: South Korean prosecutors arrest Hanbo founder.

text.p: South Korean prosecutors on Friday arrested the founder of the stricken Hanbo Group on charges of illegally issuing cheques and violating the law on mutual trust and savings companies, a prosecution official said.
The arrest of Chung Tae-soo, made during the prime news hour, was broadcast live by state television.
Investigators took Chung to a car which whisked him away to a Seoul jail.

The arrest was made at the prosecutors' office where Chung had been questioned over massive loans to the financially shaky steelmaking flagship of Hanbo Group since being summoned from a Seoul hospital on Thursday.
Hanbo Steel Co, the nation's second largest steelmaker, defaulted on debt repayments last week after piling up five trillion won ($5.8 billion) in loans from 61 banks and financial institutions.
Government officials have said the company will be rescued.
